title: SK Hynix defends its HBM bit allocation against rising DRAM prices by Q1 2027
body:
SK Hynix's second-quarter results, reported on Wednesday, July 29, describe a supplier that chose contracted high-bandwidth memory over the commodity cycle and was marked down for it. Revenue was 79.32 trillion won, about 54.5 billion dollars, up 257% against the same quarter a year earlier and up 51% against the first quarter. Operating profit was 60.54 trillion won, about 42 billion dollars, up 557% against the same quarter a year earlier, and the fifth consecutive quarter in which the company has set an operating-profit record. Analysts had modelled roughly 64.22 trillion won of operating profit, so the record still read as a miss, and the shares closed 9.6% lower in Seoul at 1.407 million won, with the US-listed line down about 3.5%. The stated reason is allocation rather than demand: SK Hynix did not manufacture enough DRAM to capture the full benefit of rising DRAM prices, because those bits went into HBM instead. Mass production and shipment of HBM4 began during the quarter and expands through the second half, HBM4E samples have gone to major customers, and the revenue mix now runs 73% DRAM and HBM against 27% NAND.

The prediction is that SK Hynix does not correct this. Through the second half of 2026 and across the two reporting rounds that follow, it keeps routing bits into the HBM4 ramp it has already described rather than pulling capacity back to harvest DRAM pricing, and it defends the choice in its own disclosure — restating the argument management made on July 29, that more efficient models lower the barrier to entry for AI applications and expand usage, which raises memory demand rather than reducing it, and pointing again at the roughly ten long-term supply agreements it says underwrite visibility into AI infrastructure spending beyond 2027. Those agreements are the reason to expect persistence rather than reversal: contracted volume is committed volume, and a supplier cannot redirect it toward a rising spot price without breaking the commitments that bought the visibility in the first place. The observable form is a company that keeps naming the allocation, not demand, as the reason its reported numbers sit below what a DRAM-cycle model produces — and that keeps making the same allocation anyway.

reasoning.because: SK Hynix fed bits to HBM instead of DRAM, set a record operating profit and still missed consensus.
reasoning.given: Ten or so long-term supply agreements commit the volume; contracted bits cannot chase a spot price.
reasoning.so_that: HBM4 ramps through the second half as planned and the gap against DRAM-cycle consensus recurs instead of closing.
reasoning.landing: by Q1 2027; SK Hynix restates it in its own results, not via a customer
reasoning.plain_language: SK Hynix is turning normal memory chips into AI memory chips. Investors wanted the normal kind. It will keep choosing AI memory.

summary: SK Hynix set a fifth straight operating-profit record in the second quarter and still missed consensus, because bits went into HBM rather than DRAM at rising prices. Expect it to hold that allocation through the HBM4 ramp and defend it at the next results rather than pull capacity back.
